accuracy.evidence: Terms checked against the National Curriculum English Appendix 2 and its glossary: Year 4 'noun phrases expanded by the addition of modifying adjectives, nouns and preposition phrases (e.g. the strict maths teacher with curly hair)'; a preposition links a following noun phrase to another word; a phrase has no verb of its own while a clause does; after/before/because can be conjunctions opening clauses. CCSS L.4.1e wording checked. Every tag in the spot scene (determiner, noun, adjective, verb, pronoun, preposition) verified word by word.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS2 slips: every place phrase treated as an adverbial (on the hill tells which house), phrases placed before the noun, clauses such as after we ate lunch called phrases, bare noun phrases called expanded, determiners or nouns taken for the preposition, and misplaced phrases that give a sentence two meanings (the telescope sentence).

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanics belong to this grammar point: a picture of four dogs where each adjective or prepositional phrase greys out the dogs it rules out, an arrow from each phrase to the noun or verb it modifies, one ambiguous sentence whose phrase is dropped on 'saw' or 'dog' to match two drawings and then moved to the front, and word tiles where the preposition opens a bracketed phrase. The shingle check passes against every other lab, including flag_fire.js and flag_nph.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the idea before it is named: the dog picture shows that 'the dog' fits four dogs and each phrase narrows it to one; the job scene draws the arrow to the word modified; the two pictures show the ambiguity, then the fronted rewrite removes it. Wrong moves explain the slip (e.g. 'after we ate lunch has a verb, ate, so it is a clause').

predictions.evidence: Prediction 1 tempts 'Just one' for how many dogs 'the dog' could mean; the picture shows four candidates until three details are added. Prediction 2 tempts 'Where something happened' for on the hill in 'The house on the hill is empty'; the lab draws the arrow to house and names the adjective job.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; each wrong option has a tagged message naming the slip: no preposition picked, place phrase assumed to mean where, bare noun phrase, phrase before the noun, clause with a verb, which-one vs where for at the park.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 1.9 with short sentences and concrete examples; adult text FK 8.1 (family limits 5.0/10.0). Grammar terms (preposition, noun phrase, adjective job, clause) are each introduced with an example the first time they appear, as the curriculum expects for Year 4.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one idea: what a prepositional phrase is, expanding a noun phrase, the two jobs, position and phrase vs clause. Adult paragraphs give standards, the two jobs with examples, named mistakes and the lab. Content gate: no filler, under 12% overlap with 406 and 276.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px canvas screenshots in light and dark: word tiles are at least 40 px tall and wrap centred; the four dogs sit in a 2 by 2 grid with the target ringed and ruled-out dogs greyed; zones were enlarged so placed phrases read at 12 px or more; the telescope pictures and sentence tiles fit without clipping. Gates use a light stroke in dark mode.

accessibility.evidence: Every move has a button: one button per word in the spot scene (aria-label gives the word and its position), Choose then a target for every card, including 'on saw' / 'on dog' for the two-meaning sentence, and Cancel. Each action updates the canvas aria-label and live region, the challenge included. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations.
